# ABS codes and how to pull 'em

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Drive over 30 km/h, then pull codes via terminal 9 and verify repairs using the Malfunction Code/Symptom Chart. [t1278]

Disconnect both terminals of the battery, wait at least 10 minutes before touching airbag system components. [t1280]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Disconnect both terminals of the battery.
2. Wait at least 10 minutes before touching the airbag system components.
3. Turn the ignition switch ON.
4. After the AIR BAG warning lamp lights for 7 seconds, turn the ignition switch OFF within 1 second.
5. Wait more than 3 seconds.
6. [Partial] Repeat steps one through three exactly three times to enter diagnosis mode.
7. Turn the ignition switch ON again to view flashing codes.

_Procedure reported by [t1280]. Photos of this job are in the source: <https://www.xterranation.org/index.php?threads/airbag-codes-and-how-to-pull-em.1643/>_

## Tips & gotchas

- Note that if one or more wheels spin on a rough road for 40 seconds, the ABS lamp illuminates but does not necessarily indicate a malfunction. [t1278]
- If using short-circuit codes (25, 21, 31, and 35), ensure the warning lamp goes out while driving after repair. [t1278]
- Connect the battery positive terminal first to minimize sparking. [t1280]
- Ensure all connectors are securely connected and wiring is complete. [t1280]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Replacing the ABS control unit immediately when code '57' appears due to low voltage instead of checking power supply first. [t1278]
- [Partial] Ignoring a potential bad ground on the ABS motor if trouble code '61' is present. [t1278]
